events.title: Trinity's capture turns into a massacre
events.summary: The raid on Room 303 begins as a textbook arrest and ends as a slaughter. Trinity submits to the squad's guns, but the instant the Big Cop reaches to cuff her she moves faster than they can follow and kills them one after another until she is the only one left standing, dropping a single 'Shit' as her only crack. Outside, the Agents arrive and strip the Lieutenant of his authority, and Smith informs him that the two units he trusted to be winning are already dead.
events.action: The squad breaches Room 303 and forces Trinity to submit; the Big Cop steps in to cuff her and she turns the arrest into a close-quarters killing, ending with every officer dead. Simultaneously the Agents displace the Lieutenant outside and Smith reveals the units are already gone.

affects_outside.enables: The massacre proves to the Agents that ordinary law enforcement cannot contain Trinity, clearing the way for them to take the operation over and pursue her themselves — Smith's move into the hotel is the direct institutional consequence of the squad's failure.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It costs the police their entire unit and their authority over the case; the Lieutenant's territorial gamble is spent, and the ordinary world's belief that this is a catchable 'little girl' is destroyed along with the officers who held it.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The wider police operation and whatever command sent the Agents now have to answer for a wiped-out unit and a target that has proven beyond their control — the deaths Smith reports are the first ripple of a pursuit that will no longer be theirs to run.

events.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
events.summary: Morpheus confirms Trinity's hotel hardline is cut and directs her to a phone at Wells and Lake. She runs the building's exterior to the street — hall, fire escape, roof, across the rooftops, and down through a window into a back stairwell — while the Agents pursue and match her. She reaches a ringing booth on the street and is gone before a garbage truck crushes it, so the Agents are left with wreckage and no body, but with the crew's next target named as Neo.
events.action: After Morpheus confirms the hotel hardline is cut and directs her to a phone at Wells and Lake, Trinity bursts into the hall into Agent Brown and his police unit and flees she plummets through the shattered glass and onto the fire escape. Finding Agent Smith waiting in the alley below, she climbs to the roof and runs the rooftops, clearing a 40-foot gap the cops cannot follow while Agent Brown duplicates the leap with the same unnatural grace. She launches from the roof's edge toward a lit window, dives, crashes through glass into a back stairwell, and — finding only wind where she expects Brown — gets to her feet despite her injuries. On the street she races a U-turning garbage truck to a ringing phone booth, answers it, and is gone before the truck pulverizes the booth; the Agents inspect the wreckage with no body, but leave with the next target named as Neo.

What she cannot see is that her clean-looking escape is feeding the machine: the very run that saves her is the thread that leads the Agents to Neo.

events.title: Neo is summoned and drawn toward the truth
events.summary: Alone in his apartment one night, Neo is contacted through his own PC by an unseen party that types messages the machine should not produce, ending with 'Follow the white rabbit' — and, on cue, a real knock answers the screen. He runs a disk-for-cash deal with Choi and Dujour as usual, but after the visitors leave he can no longer trust whether he is awake or dreaming. Dujour's small white rabbit pin then pulls him out against his better judgment, and at a crowded apartment gathering Trinity — a woman who names herself as the Trinity who breached the I.R.S. database — tells him she was on his computer, warns that he is being watched and in danger, and refuses to give him the answer because it has to be seen to be believed; when Neo asks 'What is the Matrix?' she says the answer is out there and will find him, then withdraws and leaves him standing amid the crowd as a sound closes over him.
events.action: The screen at Neo's PC blanks and types its own messages — 'Wake up, Neo,' 'The Matrix has you,' 'Follow the white rabbit,' 'Knock, knock, Neo' — and a real knock meets the last one. Still unnerved, Neo keeps the chain on, retrieves a disk from a hollowed Baudrillard, takes Choi's 'two grand,' and completes the sale. After Choi jokes the night is mescaline and that he needs to 'unplug,' Neo is hit by a returning 'feeling of unrealness' and asks whether Choi has ever been unsure he was awake. He refuses Dujour's invitation because he has work tomorrow, until he spots a small white rabbit pin on her jacket, at which 'the room tilts' and he agrees to go. At the gathering, Trinity walks straight up to him, names herself as 'the Trinity who breached the I.R.S. D-Base,' confirms she was on his computer, warns that he is 'in danger' and 'being watched,' and, pressing close in the deafening industrial music, tells him he is 'looking for an answer' that must be seen to be believed; Neo voices 'What is the Matrix?' and she says the answer is 'out there,' that it will find him, then melts into the shifting wall of bodies as a sound presses in on him.

Neo sees Agent Smith leading cops onto the floor and a female employee pointing out his cubicle, and he follows Morpheus's instructions out of the row and into an empty office. Morpheus directs him out to a ledge from which he can reach the roof; Neo commits, but his nerve breaks when the wind blasts him and the phone falls from his grip just as a cop opens the door, and he climbs back inside into the hands of the waiting cop. Morpheus's remote guidance gets him out of the row but cannot steady his body at the ledge, and the dropped phone severs his only link to that guidance at the moment he most needs it. events.title: Neo is interrogated and implanted
events.summary: Seen through a camera monitor that the viewpoint passes through like a window, Neo is led into a white interrogation room where Agent Smith lays out his two lives from a manila file labeled "Anderson, Thomas A." and offers to wipe his crimes clean in exchange for Morpheus. Neo refuses with contempt, gives Smith the finger and demands his phone call. Smith drops the negotiation, has the standing Agents pin Neo to the chair and rip open his shirt, and turns a fiber-optic wire tap into an insect/fluke-worm creature that burrows into Neo's navel. Neo's lips soften, seal and meld until his mouth is gone, leaving him mouthless, exposed and implanted — fully in the Agents' control.

Smith enjoys the performance of reasonableness — the file, the 'fresh start,' the 'He thinks you desire to act correctly.' — because it lets him frame coercion as choice. Neo's refusal does not anger him; it merely ends the charade. His certainty comes from knowing he controls the very rules of the room, so compliance was never in question, only the manner of extracting it.

events.title: Neo is reclaimed and taken to Morpheus
events.summary: A ringing phone drags Neo out of a nightmare and a voice names him 'the One,' extracting a single 'Yes' and a destination before the line dies. He crosses the rain-soaked night to the Adams Street bridge, where a car slides to a stop and Trinity pulls him inside. Under Switch's gun, Neo resists the demand to strip for an unknown device and nearly bolts, but Trinity reframes the danger as coming from himself and warns him against a road he already knows — and he closes the door and stays. The car speeds through the dark wet streets with Neo seated, silent, and no longer resisting.

state_triples.reading: Neo moves through the event as a man being reclaimed by a destiny he never asked for and still cannot comprehend. Each surrender is framed — by Morpheus's prophecy, by Trinity's gentleness — as a choice, and he accepts the framing because the alternative (the road he knows, the abyss he has always been running toward) is more terrifying than compliance. He closes the door not out of trust but because staying feels marginally less like falling; the event's quiet horror is that his one act of 'agency' is the surrender of his agency.

physical.exit: Seated in the moving car, silent, staring into the rain — no longer fighting, carried forward into the wet underworld.

events.title: The Bug Removed
events.summary: In the moving car, Trinity seals an extraction device over Neo's navel to pull a tracking bug from his body. When the gentler suction fails and Switch warns the bug is on the move, Trinity overrides Neo's pain and electrocutes him, driving the fluke-like parasite out through the machine's coils. Neo, stunned that the creature is real, watches Trinity cage it; the car then vanishes into the rainy night and comes to a stop a lonely lane behind a long-abandoned hotel.
events.action: The extraction shifts from persuasion to force. Trinity first tries to coax the bug out with suction while reassuring Neo, but the monitor shows it burrowing deeper and Switch keeps announcing that she is about to lose it. She refuses to let it escape, fires an electric charge into Neo, and holds it through his convulsions until the bug rockets free. Trinity then displays the squirming creature to Neo, rolls down the window, and discards it; the car carries the crew out of the wet streets, vanishing into the rainy night before pulling up behind a forgotten hotel.

state_triples.reading: Neo's terror is less about the pain than about the violation of his own interior slithering beneath his skin; when the bug rockets out he is appalled that his body was secretly colonized, and the shock lands as the first real crack in everything he believed about how the world works. He cannot yet know Trinity's cruelty was a desperate medical necessity, so he reads her as someone who hurt him with casual intent — and that misreading binds him to her even as it keeps him wary.

events.title: Born Into the Real World
events.summary: The machine unplugs Neo: it spins open the coaxial lock at the base of his skull, withdraws the clear plastic needle and cerebrum-chip from the front of his skull, and releases the tether holding him to the pod. Freed, Neo ruptures the shroud and tears out of his cell, then is flushed through the plant's waste lines and nearly drowns before a metallic cable lifts him into a flying machine that carries him aboard the hovercraft. A harness sets him down, hands raise him to face Morpheus, who names him and welcomes him to the real world, and Neo passes out.
events.action: The machine spins the cable lock open at the base of Neo's skull and the coaxial disengages; the clear plastic needle and cerebrum-chip slide out of the anterior of his skull, and the main hard-lock tether releases him from the pod. The harness opens and drops him half-conscious onto the hovercraft floor; hands lift him to face Morpheus, who names him and welcomes him to the real world, and Neo collapses and passes out.

events.title: Waking and Rebuilding
events.summary: Neo surfaces from unconsciousness into Morpheus's custody on the hovercraft and is carried through three stages: a first waking where Morpheus answers his fear of death with certainty, a surgical rebuilding in the infirmary where his atrophied body is repaired and his questions met with measured truth, and a third waking in his own room where the discovery of grafted hardware and the loss of two centuries knock him off balance. Morpheus refuses to explain further and instead leads him, a passenger being shown rather than told, up through the ship toward the main deck.
events.action: Neo wakes on the hovercraft floor to Morpheus's face haloed by a light stick and asks whether he is dead; Morpheus tells him he is far from it. In the infirmary Neo wakes again to find his body studded with acupuncture-like needles wired to a device while Dozer reports his condition and Morpheus operates; Morpheus explains his muscles have atrophied and are being rebuilt, and that his eyes hurt because he has never used them, then tells him to rest because the answers are coming. Neo wakes a final time in his own room, pulls a futuristic IV from a jack in his forearm, finds an outlet grafted into the base of his skull, and as he begins to come unglued Morpheus enters; Morpheus redirects his questions from what to when, telling him he believes the year is 1997 when it is closer to 2197, admitting no one truly knows the exact year. Neo follows Morpheus like a sleepwalker through the ship as Morpheus names it the Nebuchadnezzar, and they ascend the ladder to the main deck.

affects_outside.enables: By rebuilding Neo's body and reorienting his mind, the event makes it possible for Morpheus to proceed to a direct demonstration of reality — Neo must be whole enough and present enough to be shown rather than merely told.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: Morpheus's choice to show rather than explain, and to defer the full truth, forecloses the gentler path of gradual briefing and commits him to a revelation that will overwhelm Neo to the point of rejection.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Trinity's unresolved doubt hangs over the event from off-page; her protective skepticism is the caution Morpheus overrides, and it stands ready to be vindicated if his certainty about Neo proves misplaced.

events.turns_on: Morpheus's decision to show Neo the truth rather than explain it — the pivot from telling to showing that converts Neo's reorientation into a direct, unmediated confrontation with reality, as he leads a rebuilt but shaken Neo toward witnessing rather than being told.

prose_before_reconcile.action: Neo wakes to Morpheus's face haloed by a light stick and asks whether he is dead; Morpheus tells him he is far from it. In the infirmary Neo wakes again to find his body studded with acupuncture-like needles wired to a device while Dozer and Morpheus operate on him; Morpheus explains his muscles have atrophied and are being rebuilt, and that his eyes hurt because he has never used them, then closes his eyes and tells him to rest because the answers are coming. Neo wakes a final time in his own room, pulls a futuristic IV from a jack in his forearm, finds an outlet grafted into the base of his skull, and as he begins to come unglued Morpheus enters; Morpheus redirects his questions from what to when, telling him he believes the year is 1997 when it is closer to 2197, admitting no one truly knows the exact year. Neo follows Morpheus like a sleepwalker through the ship as Morpheus names it the Nebuchadnezzar, a hovercraft small like a submarine, cramped and cold but home, and they ascend the ladder to the main deck.
